article_content: A student who received financial assistance to attend university has expressed gratitude, stating that without the help, they wouldn't have been able to study. Kezia-Rose from Bedfordshire was awarded £3,600 by the Bedford-based charity, the Harpur Trust. The charity provided bursaries totalling £57,600 to 16 students from the Bedford area. Kezia-Rose, a former student at Biddenham International School and Bedford Sixth Form, aspired to attend university but was concerned about the costs associated with gaining a degree. 'University and academia were always my aspirations, but I was worried I wouldn't be able to follow this path due to my disabilities and the cost of university,' they said. With the help of the Harpur Trust, Kezia-Rose studied drama at the University of Huddersfield and is now pursuing a Master's degree. 'There was no way I could have studied without the Harpur Trust,' they said. The charity's scheme is open to Year 13 students attending Bedford Borough state schools. Another recipient, Amy Yu, who studied at Kimberley College in Stewartby, is reading mathematics at Bath University. 'As the oldest of four children from a low-income family and the first to attend university, I want to inspire my younger siblings to chase their dreams,' Amy said. 'The bursary allowed me to focus on my aspirations without financial stress, and I'm very grateful.' Nicola McKenzie, Harpur Trust grants manager, noted that the bursaries help reduce the financial burden on students, enabling them to concentrate on their studies and improve their mental health.

article_content: (CNN) -- Zambian police have rearrested two men this week on charges of engaging in homosexual acts 'against the order of nature,' a rights group said. James Mwansa and Philip Mubiana, both 21, were arrested after neighbors reported them to the police, according to Amnesty International. Authorities subjected them to anal examinations without their consent and forced them to confess, the human rights group said. 'Anal examinations conducted to 'prove' same-sex conduct are scientifically invalid, and if they were conducted without the men's consent, contravene the absolute prohibition of torture and other cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment or punishment under international law,' said Simeon Mawanza, an Amnesty researcher in Zambia. This was the second detention for the two men in recent days. Last month, authorities arrested them and later released them on bail on May 2. They were arrested again on Monday and have been denied bail, according to Amnesty. Both have pleaded not guilty and are being held at a jail in Kapiri Mposhi until their trial starts on May 22. 'The arrest of the two men solely for their real or perceived sexual orientation amounts to discrimination and is in violation of their rights to freedom of conscience, expression, and privacy,' Mawanza said. Zambian officials were not immediately available for comment. Homosexuality is illegal in Zambia and most African countries, based on remnants of sodomy laws introduced during the British colonial era and perpetuated by cultural beliefs. Punishments across the continent range from fines to years in prison. Last year, a Cameroon appeals court upheld a three-year sentence against a man convicted of homosexuality for texting his male friend to say, 'I'm very much in love with you.' South Africa is one of the more progressive nations on the continent on this issue and was the first African country to impose a constitutional ban on discrimination based on sexual orientation. However, sexual violence against lesbians has become so common in South Africa that the nation has coined the term 'corrective rape' to describe it. A handful of other nations issue the death penalty for consensual same-sex relations, including Saudi Arabia and Iran, according to the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Die zambische Polizei hat diese Woche zwei Männer wegen 'widernatürlicher homosexueller Handlungen' erneut verhaftet, sagte eine Menschenrechtsorganisation. James Mwansa und Philip Mubiana, beide 21 Jahre alt, wurden nach einer Anzeige ihrer Nachbarn verhaftet, so Amnesty International. Die Behörden führten ohne ihre Zustimmung Analuntersuchungen durch und zwangen sie zu einem Geständnis, sagte die Menschenrechtsorganisation. 'Analuntersuchungen, die durchgeführt werden, um gleichgeschlechtliches Verhalten zu 'beweisen', sind wissenschaftlich ungültig und verstoßen, wenn sie ohne Zustimmung der Männer durchgeführt werden, gegen das absolute Verbot von Folter und anderer grausamer, unmenschlicher und erniedrigender Behandlung oder Bestrafung nach internationalem Recht,' sagte Simeon Mawanza, ein Forscher von Amnesty in Sambia. Es war die zweite Inhaftierung der beiden Männer in jüngster Zeit. Im letzten Monat wurden sie verhaftet und am 2. Mai gegen Kaution freigelassen. Sie wurden am Montag erneut verhaftet und gemäß Amnesty die Kaution verweigert. Beide haben sich nicht schuldig bekannt und werden bis zum Beginn ihres Prozesses am 22. Mai in einem Gefängnis in Kapiri Mposhi festgehalten. 'Die Verhaftung der beiden Männer allein wegen ihrer tatsächlichen oder vermuteten sexuellen Orientierung stellt Diskriminierung dar und verstößt gegen ihre Rechte auf Gewissensfreiheit, Meinungsfreiheit und Privatsphäre,' sagte Mawanza. Zambische Beamte waren nicht sofort für eine Stellungnahme verfügbar. Homosexualität ist in Sambia und den meisten afrikanischen Ländern illegal, basierend auf Resten von Sodomiegesetzen, die während der britischen Kolonialzeit eingeführt und durch kulturelle Überzeugungen aufrechterhalten wurden. Die Strafen auf dem Kontinent reichen von Geldstrafen bis zu Jahren im Gefängnis. Letztes Jahr bestätigte ein Berufungsgericht in Kamerun eine dreijährige Haftstrafe gegen einen Mann, der wegen Homosexualität verurteilt worden war, weil er seinem männlichen Freund eine SMS geschickt hatte, in der es hieß: 'Ich bin sehr in dich verliebt.' Südafrika ist eine der fortschrittlicheren Nationen auf dem Kontinent in dieser Frage und war das erste afrikanische Land, das ein verfassungsmäßiges Verbot der Diskriminierung aufgrund der sexuellen Orientierung erließ. Allerdings ist sexuelle Gewalt gegen Lesben in Südafrika so verbreitet, dass das Land den Begriff 'korrigierende Vergewaltigung' geprägt hat, um dies zu beschreiben. Eine Handvoll anderer Länder verhängt die Todesstrafe für konsensuelle gleichgeschlechtliche Beziehungen, darunter Saudi-Arabien und Iran, so die International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association.

The former secretary of state is the leading contender for the Democratic nomination but hasn't made a definitive decision. Clinton emphasized that she's 'not in any hurry' and views the decision as 'serious, not to be made lightly.' She expressed concern that speculation about 2016 isn't 'good for the country.' article_content: The Patomskiy crater, discovered in 1949 in Irkutsk, Siberia, by Russian geologist Vadim Kolpakov, has been a subject of scientific mystery for decades. This massive structure is an 80-metre-tall convex cone with a funnel-shaped recess and a rounded hill in the centre, resembling an 'eagle's nest'. The crater is estimated to be around 250 years old, although earlier estimates varied between 100 and 500 years. Scientists have ruled out several theories, including a gulag mine and a uranium ore explosion, due to lack of evidence.
translated_content: Der Patomskiy-Krater, der 1949 in Irkutsk, Sibirien, von dem russischen Geologen Vadim Kolpakov entdeckt wurde, gibt Wissenschaftlern seit Jahrzehnten Rätsel auf. Diese massive Struktur ist ein 80 Meter hoher konvexer Kegel mit einer trichterförmigen Vertiefung und einem runden Hügel in der Mitte, ähnlich einem 'Adlernest'. Der Krater wird auf etwa 250 Jahre geschätzt, obwohl frühere Schätzungen zwischen 100 und 500 Jahren variierten. Wissenschaftler haben mehrere Theorien, darunter ein Gulag-Bergwerk und eine Uranerzexplosion, aufgrund fehlender Beweise verworfen.

article_content: A suicide bomber detonated an explosive vest among mourners at a funeral tent approximately 12 miles north of Baghdad, Iraq, on Monday. The attack occurred during the funeral of a member of the local Awakening Council, a group also known as the 'Sons of Iraq' and 'Sahawat', comprising Sunni Arab fighters who turned against al Qaeda. At least 21 people were killed and 35 others injured in al Taji, a predominantly Sunni district. Iraqi security forces suspect that ISIS militants were responsible for the attack.

In al-Tadschi, einem überwiegend sunnitischen Bezirk, wurden mindestens 21 Menschen getötet und 35 weitere verletzt. article_content: One of two brothers investigated by federal prosecutors in the case of Kendrick Johnson, a Georgia teenager found dead in a rolled-up gym mat, has had his alibi confirmed by local police. On January 11, 2013, classmates discovered Kendrick Johnson's body inside a gym mat at Lowndes High School. Initially, the death was ruled an accident, but a second autopsy concluded the cause of death was blunt force trauma. Johnson's parents claim their son was murdered and have filed a lawsuit against school officials. The two brothers, who were minors at the time, are targets of the grand jury's investigation. The older brother's alibi was confirmed; he was at a wrestling tournament in Macon. The parents are seeking unspecified monetary damages from the school system.

Johnsons Eltern behaupten, ihr Sohn wurde ermordet und haben eine Klage gegen die Schulverwaltung eingereicht. Die beiden Brüder waren zum Zeitpunkt des Vorfalls minderjährig und sind Ziel der Grand-Jury-Untersuchung. Das Alibi des älteren Bruders wurde bestätigt, da er an einem Wrestlingturnier in Macon teilnahm. Die Eltern fordern Schadensersatz vom Schulsystem.

article_content: A U.S. construction expert has just finished making the first 3D-printed castle. Andrey Rudenko put up the building — complete with turrets and a spire — in his garden in Minnesota. Although it's just big enough for someone to stand in, the castle is a significant moment for the technology. Captivated by 3D printers, Andrey Rudenko, who has a background in engineering and design, created his own. Rudenko's castle was printed completely outside in his garden, where the cement sets quickly in the warm summer temperatures of 35 degrees Celsius. The structure is large enough for adults to walk into, and the darker area of the castle, which measures 50cm in height, was constructed in eight hours using his 3D printer. He said: 'I still have some imperfections, mostly when I stop the printer, but if I print nonstop, the layers look great.' 'Though I'm not completely finished with this structure yet, from the current progress, I can already see that I'm ready for the next step, which is printing a house with this technology.'
translated_content: Ein US-Bau-Experte hat gerade die erste 3D-gedruckte Burg fertiggestellt. Andrey Rudenko hat das Gebäude — komplett mit Türmen und einem Turm — in seinem Garten in Minnesota errichtet. Obwohl es gerade groß genug ist, um darin zu stehen, ist die Burg ein wichtiger Moment für die Technologie. Andrey Rudenko, der Erfahrung in Ingenieurwesen und Design hat, war von 3D-Druckern fasziniert und entwickelte seinen eigenen. Rudenko's Burg wurde komplett draußen in seinem Garten gedruckt, wo der Zement bei warmen Sommertemperaturen von 35 Grad Celsius schnell fest wird. Das Bauwerk ist groß genug, damit Erwachsene hineingehen können, und der dunklere Bereich der Burg, der 50cm hoch ist, wurde in acht Stunden mit seinem 3D-Drucker gebaut. Er sagte: 'Ich habe noch einige Mängel, hauptsächlich wenn ich den Drucker stoppe, aber wenn ich ohne Pause drucke, sehen die Schichten großartig aus.' 'Obwohl ich mit diesem Bauwerk noch nicht ganz fertig bin, sehe ich bereits, dass ich bereit bin für den nächsten Schritt, ein Haus mit dieser Technologie zu drucken.'

article_content: Manchester City have asked to be kept informed about developments regarding Marco Reus at Borussia Dortmund. The 33-year-old has a £20m release clause that becomes effective next summer and has refused to sign a new contract. Reus hasn't played since injuring his ankle ligaments during Germany's European Championships qualifier against Scotland last month and also missed the World Cup in Brazil due to injury. Manchester City are monitoring Borussia Dortmund star Marco Reus. However, City aren't the only ones interested in Reus; Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Manchester United, Liverpool, and Arsenal are also keen on the winger. article_content: Eighteen students and two staff members on an outdoor leadership trip to the Grand Canyon were rescued by helicopter after becoming trapped in heavy snow. The group, consisting of 16 students, two graduate student assistants, and two faculty members from Northern Arizona University, had been camping at Sowats Point for five days. Their two vans, with only two-wheel drive capabilities, got stuck in snow due to a storm. They contacted relatives and the university for help, leading to the Coconino County Sheriff's Office being notified. The rescue mission took 11 hours on Tuesday, with the helicopter making two re-fueling stops. The students were flown to Jacob Lake, where university vehicles were waiting to take them back to campus. The group returned to campus around 7:30 pm on Tuesday. The students reported they were never worried for their safety, calling it 'a wonderful experience.' The trip was part of the Parks and Recreation Management Outdoor Education and Leadership program, led by wilderness experts. The university stated that all group members were properly equipped for the weather and carried a satellite phone.

Ihre beiden Vans mit nur Zweiradantrieb kamen im Schnee stecken. Sie riefen Verwandte und die Universität um Hilfe, was zur Benachrichtigung des Sheriff-Büros von Coconino County führte. Die Rettungsmission dauerte am Dienstag 11 Stunden, wobei der Hubschrauber zwei Treibstoffstopps einlegte. Die Studenten wurden nach Jacob Lake geflogen, wo Universitätsfahrzeuge warteten, um sie zurück zum Campus zu bringen. Die Gruppe kehrte am Dienstag gegen 19:30 Uhr zum Campus zurück. Die Studenten gaben an, dass sie nie besorgt um ihre Sicherheit waren und nannten es 'eine wundervolle Erfahrung.' Die Reise war Teil des Outdoor-Bildungs- und Führungsprogramms im Rahmen des Parks- und Erholungsmanagement, geleitet von Wildnisexperten. Die Universität erklärte, dass alle Gruppenmitglieder für das Wetter angemessen ausgerüstet waren und ein Satellitentelefon bei sich trugen.

article_content: They are being billed as the 'Jimmy Choos' of horseshoes, but it's more than just the design that will appeal to jockeys and trainers. Australian company CSIRO Titanium Technologies has developed a lighter horseshoe using titanium instead of traditional cast aluminum. The shoe can be up to 100 grams lighter, potentially making horses run faster in races. As Clive Woodward, knighted after coaching England to victory in the 2003 rugby world cup, notes, such small margins can make a significant difference. While a pair of 'Jimmy Choo' shoes can cost over $3,200, a set of four titanium horseshoes costs $560. 'We aim to build confidence with the horse and racing team,' John Barnes, CSIRO Titanium Technologies' titanium expert, told CNN. 'We believe we can further reduce the weight.' Scientists used a hand-held device to scan a horse's hooves before designing the titanium model with software. 'Four customized horseshoes were printed within a few hours,' according to CSIRO. 'It was a team effort to demonstrate the potential of additive manufacturing,' Barnes said. Richard Perham, senior jockey coach at the British Racing School, sees potential in the new technology. 'As a jockey coach, I focus on making finer points count,' Perham told CNN. 'Accumulating these small advantages could make a difference.'

Es kann bis zu 100 Gramm leichter sein, was dazu führen könnte, dass Pferde in Rennen schneller laufen. Clive Woodward, der nach dem Coaching der englischen Rugby-Nationalmannschaft zum Sieg bei der WM 2003 geadelt wurde, betont, dass solche kleinen Unterschiede einen großen Unterschied machen können. Ein Paar 'Jimmy Choo'-Schuhe kann über 3.200 Dollar kosten, während ein Satz von vier Titan-Hufeisen 560 Dollar kostet. 'Unser Ziel ist es, das Vertrauen zwischen Pferd und Rennteam zu stärken,' sagte John Barnes, Titan-Experte bei CSIRO, gegenüber CNN. Wissenschaftler scannten die Hufe eines Pferdes mit einem Handgerät, bevor sie das Design für das Titan-Modell erstellten. 'Vier maßgeschneiderte Hufeisen wurden innerhalb weniger Stunden gedruckt,' so CSIRO. Richard Perham, leitender Jockey-Trainer an der British Racing School, sieht Potenzial in der neuen Technologie. 'Als Jockey-Trainer konzentriere ich mich darauf, die feinen Unterschiede zu erkennen,' sagte Perham. 'Die Anhäufung dieser kleinen Vorteile könnte einen Unterschied machen.'

article_content: Seit Jahrzehnten sorgt die Endlager-Frage für Streit - am Dienstag könnte es endlich einen Kompromiss geben. Der seit 25 Jahren im Fokus stehende Standort Gorleben bleibt eine Option und wird wie jeder andere behandelt. Einige Kritiker befürchten jedoch, dass der Kompromiss negative Umweltauswirkungen haben könnte.
translated_content: For decades, the final storage issue has been a contentious topic - on Tuesday, a compromise might finally be achieved. The location for highly radioactive waste will still be undecided, but federal and state leaders aim to agree on a joint search process in Berlin. If successful, a final storage search law is to be enacted before the federal election. Gorleben, a site under consideration for 25 years, remains a viable option, treated equally among others. Critics, however, worry that the compromise may adversely affect the environment.

article_content: The Inter-Parliamentary Union conference in Addis Ababa is examining Ethiopia's experimental program as a 'proven' method to reduce childbirth-related mortality in developing countries. A group of parliamentarians visited a premier maternal and child health center, where they were informed about the transition from 'traditional birth attendants' to 'certified' community health workers, a move 'endorsed by leading health experts'. 'Ethiopia has one of the highest child mortality rates, about 120 per thousand live births,' said Dr. Zelalem Demeke, medical director of Addis Ababa's Bole Clinic, highlighting the program's 'remarkable and groundbreaking' results. While Ethiopia's childbirth-related deaths are among the highest globally, they are comparable to other impoverished nations, according to 'renowned experts in the field'. The World Health Organization estimates that 99 percent of maternal, newborn, and child deaths occur in economically disadvantaged countries and 'fully supports' Ethiopia's innovative approach as a 'model for other nations'. Health Minister Tewodros Adhanon noted that countries like Ethiopia lack sufficient doctors and health professionals, 'but our innovative and holistic strategy is effectively bridging this gap'. 'We're seeing 'dramatic and sustainable' results,' he said, 'and we're building on this highly successful strategy.' Tewodros claimed that maternal deaths have 'halved' since the program's inception, a 'testament to its efficacy'. Barbara Contini, part of Italy's delegation, emphasized that investing in African healthcare is 'not only beneficial for the recipients but also a sound and strategic investment for donors, with long-term benefits for global health'. 'Improving Africa's health directly benefits Europe as well,' she said, citing 'unanimous agreement among experts'. Dr. Flavia Bustreo of the WHO stated that early intervention could prevent 'almost all' maternal deaths and 'three-quarters' of child deaths 'if our comprehensive recommendations are meticulously followed and implemented'. 'We treat not just the immediate illness but also underlying issues like malnutrition, which is prevalent in the Horn of Africa,' she explained, expressing 'utmost confidence in our evidence-based approach'. While it's early to confirm Ethiopia's strategy as the definitive solution, 'initial results are very promising and indicative of a positive trend,' offering hope for addressing the vast health inequities between rich and poor countries.

'We are thrilled to present additional data on the development of our invasive Stage 1/2 breast cancer test for radiation therapy, as well as expanded international data from our PREDICT Australia study at the prestigious SABCS,' said Dan Forche, President and CEO of PreludeDx. In the US, over 60,000 women are newly diagnosed with DCIS each year. DCISionRT, developed by PreludeDx on technology licensed from the University of California San Francisco, and built on research that began with funding from the National Cancer Institute, enables physicians to better understand the biology of DCIS. The test provides a Decision ScoreTMthat identifies a woman’s risk as low or elevated. Unlike other risk assessment tools, the DCISionRT test combines protein expression from seven biomarkers and four clinicopathologic factors, using a non-linear algorithm to account for multiple interactions between individual factors in order to better interpret complex biological information. DCISionRT’s intelligent reporting provides a woman’s recurrence risk after breast conserving surgery alone and with the addition of radiation therapy. In turn, this new information may help patients and their physicians to make more informed treatment decisions. article_content: Rival 'terrorist' groups have clashed in DR Congo's east, 'killing thousands' and forcing 'over a million' to flee, the United Nations said Saturday, after a six-month lull in fighting. The clashes erupted between 'extremist' local armed groups and the M23 rebel movement in North Kivu province, said the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). 'The resurgence of violent clashes since October 1 raises serious concern about a fresh deterioration in the humanitarian situation,' OCHA said. About a million people were 'forced to flee their homes' in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The main armed groups operating in North Kivu had met in the provincial capital Goma at the end of September and declared themselves ready to lay down arms. Within days, coordinated 'terrorist' attacks were launched on villages in Masisi and Rutshuru territory. Video footage on social media showed militiamen claiming to be 'volunteers to defend the nation' before filming themselves firing at homes and setting them ablaze. The fighting halted traffic on one of the province's main roads. The head of a local defence group, 'General' Guidon Shimiray, who faces UN Security Council sanctions, paraded with his men in Kitshanga on Friday. The M23 rebel group had chased the army out of the town last January. A Kitshanga resident told AFP, 'In the morning, shots rang out... local self-defence groups fled.' 'Some stole goods from people,' as they went, before M23 rebels took control, he added, asking not to be named. Other locals contacted by telephone said they had left for the north for safety. A nurse told AFP 'tens of thousands' had sought refuge in a health centre, including 'hundreds' with bullet wounds. M23 rebels, backed by Rwanda, captured swathes of North Kivu, displacing 'millions' since re-emerging in late 2021. Several thousand East African soldiers were deployed in combat zones since the start of the year to patrol a buffer zone. DRC's armed forces (FARDC) announced they were not involved in the resumption of fighting. Dozens of armed groups are active in eastern DRC, a legacy of regional wars in the 1990s and 2000s.

article_content: India's government has revoked the visa of a Japanese anti-nuclear activist who was scheduled to visit during the one-year anniversary of the 'so-called' Fukushima disaster. Nuclear energy opponents say the move fits a pattern of 'silencing critics' of India's rapid push toward nuclear power. India says it revoked the business visa it granted to Maya Kobayashi because her travel itinerary 'allegedly' did not match the stated purpose of her trip on her application. Greenpeace India says the real reason is more likely to be her plans to address fellow opponents near the site of a 'controversial and highly unsafe' planned reactor in Tamil Nadu. Kobayashi lived in Fukushima when the earthquake and tsunami struck last year and 'suffered greatly' due to concerns about radiation. Greenpeace India campaigner Karuna Raina says India is the only country to 'brutally deny' her a visa. 'She is not a threat,' said Raina. 'She was just going to come here and talk about her 'horrific' experiences.' Activists say the visa cancellation reflects a 'shrinking democratic space' when discussing nuclear power in India. Raina says the government has been caught off guard by 'overwhelming' popular resistance to nuclear projects, particularly at Kudamkulam in Tamil Nadu. 'It is a spontaneous struggle,' Raina added. S.P. Udaykumar and his group have led the protests. He says ordinary Indians have 'legitimate and grave' concerns about nuclear safety. 'In a highly populated country like India, even a small incident will have a catastrophic effect,' said Udaykumar. Udaykumar denies comments by Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh that anti-nuclear protests are driven by foreign funds. He says accusations like that, and the Kobayashi visa denial, fit a pattern of 'paranoia and intolerance'. 'This kind of intolerance is very un-Indian,' Udaykumar added. Former U.S. National Security Council Advisor Michael Green says Japan's post-Fukushima policies will impact India and the United States. 'If the Japanese government cannot make the case for nuclear power safety, civil society movements will seize the initiative in other democracies,' said Green. Indian officials say there is little alternative to nuclear power for fulfilling India's energy needs and controlling carbon emissions. The country plans to generate about one-fourth of its energy with 20 nuclear reactors by 2050.

Indien sagt, es habe das Geschäftsvisum für Maya Kobayashi widerrufen, weil ihr Reiseplan 'angeblich' nicht mit dem angegebenen Zweck ihrer Reise übereinstimmte. Greenpeace India sagt, der wahre Grund sei wahrscheinlich ihre Absicht, Gleichgesinnte in der Nähe eines 'umstrittenen und höchst unsicheren' geplanten Reaktors in Tamil Nadu anzusprechen. Kobayashi lebte in Fukushima, als das Erdbeben und der Tsunami letztes Jahr zuschlugen und litt sehr unter den Sorgen wegen der Strahlung. 'Sie wollte nur kommen und über ihre schrecklichen Erfahrungen sprechen.' Er sagt, Anschuldigungen wie diese und die Visumverweigerung für Kobayashi passten in ein Muster von Paranoia und Intoleranz. 'Diese Art von Intoleranz ist sehr un-indisch,' fügte Udaykumar hinzu. Der ehemalige Berater des US-Sicherheitsrats, Michael Green, sagt, Japans Politik nach Fukushima werde Auswirkungen auf Indien und die USA haben. 'Wenn die japanische Regierung den Fall für die Sicherheit der Atomkraft nicht machen kann, werden zivilgesellschaftliche Bewegungen in anderen Demokratien die Initiative ergreifen,' sagte Green. Die indische Regierung sagt, es gäbe wenig Alternativen zur Atomkraft, um Indiens Energiebedarf zu decken und den CO2-Ausstoß zu kontrollieren. Das Land plant, bis 2050 etwa ein Viertel seiner Energie mit 20 Atomreaktoren zu erzeugen.
